hypothesis: Explicit neutral STOP, two issued-command history and short last-seen target-side memory can reduce delayed-command and sensor-dropout failures while preserving nominal performance.
tie_break: stress success minus twice collision; then nominal mean steps
baselines: published v1 Q-table mapped explicitly to v3 actions1..5; rules; same v3 physics and supervisors for all controllers
supervision: Host and receiver check noisy observed clearances; STOP is neutral, immediate and flushes pending commands. Startup queue is neutral. Passive current still acts during STOP.
limitations: Synthetic observations and coarse range, not actual YOLO frames/depth
Normalized synthetic thrust and idealized priority STOP; no physical inertia/watchdog calibration
Fresh simulation seeds do not establish boat-field generalization
Changed schema is incompatible with the deployed 5-action Q-table; do not overwrite it
